purpose: Prevent strategy or element changes from creating a system-level failure even when the local element passes its own tests.
core_principle: Every material strategy change and every element completion triggers a fresh adversarial review of the entire approved architecture and operating model before the boundary may be VERIFIED or CLOSED.

survivability_target.name: architectural_survivability
survivability_target.meaning: No single provider, application component, deployment change, migration, operator error, policy change, legal/document change or integration ambiguity may destroy canonical truth or make recovery impossible within the designed recovery boundary.

mandatory_questions: Can the change create two authoritative values for one live business concern?
Can an external side effect happen twice after timeout_or_lost_response?
Can a provider outage or provider replacement corrupt canonical truth?
Can an operator complete a task without losing the causal link to its evidence, handoff and outcome?
Can two operators overwrite each other or act on stale state?
Can a failed migration leave the old and new systems both partially authoritative?
Can the system continue safely when a legal or EDO rule changes?
Can cost, quota, rate-limit or storage exhaustion amplify into cascading failure?
Can a new UI, integration or runtime path silently bypass an existing policy or evidence gate?
Can the system reconstruct what happened after an ambiguous external result?
Can untrusted public input amplify provider lookups or exhaust shared application resources?
Can an identifier lookup endpoint be abused as a registry enumeration oracle?
Can a public form bypass evidence, idempotency or canonical API controls and create duplicate business state?
Can a public attachment or payload become an execution, storage or denial-of-service vector?
Can a failure between the dedicated intake database and Shema lose a client request or duplicate an operator notification?
Can a repeat-order migration delete Shema state before Bitrix24 has a complete verified copy and a recoverable snapshot?
Can the operator UI hide transferred Order/Economics views without breaking navigation, deep links or causal history?
Can a monitored counterparty produce a false change event because the registry source is stale, unavailable, reordered or partially updated?
Can attacker-controlled client text poison an AI prompt, operator notification or Bitrix24 business field?
Can a compromised integration credential or Bitrix24 app gain authority beyond its owned namespace?
Can the operator interface expose or imply a business authority that Shema does not own?
Can capability removal after Bitrix24 cutover leave a stale navigation entry, deep link, cache entry or empty workspace that exposes obsolete business state?
Can personal view preferences, saved filters or Kanban interactions bypass server-side authorization or concurrency protection?
